summary: A 249-line self-contained Coq file (only `Require Import Setoid`) encoding the CNs-as-setoids account of individuation and copredication from Chatzikyriakidis & Luo 2020, ch.5 (s.5.3) and s.6.3.2. Lines 1-236 are a near-verbatim copy of the book's own Appendix A7.9 'Individuation' (pp. 200-207): the same records Equiv/Equiv_K/CN/CN_K, the same ontology (Human, Man, Phy, Info, Book, the PhyInfo record standing in for the dot-type PHY.INFO, the Sigma-records Heavybook and Heavyinfobook), the same identity-criterion (IC) inheritance definitions AIC_*/IC_*/capitalised setoids, and 19 of the file's 20 theorems including copred_dd1/copred_dd2, which verify the chapter's headline double-distinctness inference (6.3)/(5.47)-(5.48). The only edits are the renamings three_0 -> three_f and three -> three_c, five dropped and one added comment. Lines 238-249 are the file's own tail: the s.5.4 typing of the Liebesman & Magidor example (5.79) (OTS, WL, WaP) as two `Check`s, a quantifier `one` that is a byte-for-byte duplicate of `some`, and one trivial new theorem threedf (three -> one). All 20 theorems are Qed, 0 Admitted, 0 propositional axioms (two function-typed Axioms mh, bf serve as coercion witnesses); compiles under Coq 8.20.1. Faithful to the book's own Coq; the gaps relative to the chapter-5 theory (no generic THREE(A,B,P) with A <= B -- three_c has a phantom type argument and hard-codes Book/IC_PhyInfo; adjective cases (5.54)/(5.60) proved only in single-IC form; HIBook Sigma-nesting reversed vs (5.58); no dot-type formation constraint; no IC-respecting-predicate requirement; HEAVYIBOOK2 duplicating HEAVYBOOK2) are all inherited from A7.9. Byte-identical (modulo trailing newline) to ttr_mtt/Book_Individuation.v; extras/indi.v is the copy Required by extras/mass.v.

sources.citation: Chatzikyriakidis, S. & Luo, Z. (2020). Formal Semantics in Modern Type Theories. ISTE/Wiley. Relevant: ch.5 'Copredication and Individuation' -- s.5.2 dot-types (Def 5.1 components, formation rule with C(A) cap C(B) = empty, (5.11)-(5.12)), s.5.3 (5.13) setoids, (5.15), s.5.3.1 (5.21)-(5.26) and Def 5.2 sub-setoid, s.5.3.2 Def 5.3 Three_0 (5.27) and Def 5.4 Three (5.34), s.5.3.3 (5.41)-(5.48) with Def 5.5 pre-setoids and Def 5.6 THREE, s.5.3.4 (5.49)-(5.60) adjectives; s.5.4 pp. 122-125 Liebesman & Magidor (5.69)-(5.80), fn 14; s.6.3.2 'Copredication and individuation in Coq' pp. 146-149, (6.3), (6.4), fn 12 p.142; Appendix A7.9 'Individuation' pp. 200-207 (the direct textual origin of l.1-236); Appendix 6 rules for dot-types.

Luo, Z. (2012). Common Nouns as Types. LACL 2012, LNCS 7351, pp. 173-185. Cited by the book (s.5.3 p.109, as Luo 2012a) as the origin of the 'CN = type + identity criterion' proposal; background only, the file encodes nothing specific to it.

definitions_mapped.coq: Definition DomCN := Set (l.3)
definitions_mapped.source: A7.9 p.200 `Definition DomCN:=Set.`; s.6.3.2 p.147 'the old CN universe is replaced by DomCN'; universe CN of s.2.3.2; fn 12 p.142 'Coq does not allow us to specify new universes ... so we use Set to define CN, although CN should have been a separate universe'
definitions_mapped.note: Exact to the book's Coq, but relative to the theory a universe collapse: every Set is a CN domain. Probe: `Check three_c nat` type-checks as `(PhyInfo -> Prop) -> Prop`.

definitions_mapped.coq: Record Equiv (A:DomCN) : Type := mkEquiv {eq1 :> A->A->Prop; _eq2 : reflexive A eq1 /\ symmetric A eq1 /\ transitive A eq1} (l.6-7)
definitions_mapped.source: (5.13) setoid (A, =) with = : A -> A -> Prop an equivalence relation; A7.9 p.200 verbatim; s.6.3.2 p.147
definitions_mapped.note: The relation field is a coercion, so `IC_Human x y` reads as the book's x =h y. Being Type-valued, an Equiv A is always inhabited (probe: Leibniz eq gives `Equiv Human`), so declaring IC_* as Parameters adds no propositional strength.

definitions_mapped.coq: Record Equiv_K (A:DomCN) : Type := mkEquiv_K {eq2 :> A->A->Prop; _eq3 : reflexive A eq2 /\ symmetric A eq2} (l.8-9)
definitions_mapped.source: Def 5.5(1) pre-setoid (A, kappa_A), kappa_A reflexive and symmetric (p.115); A7.9 p.200 verbatim
definitions_mapped.note: s.6.3.2 p.148 calls this 'the partial equivalence relation K', a misnomer (a PER is symmetric+transitive); the record correctly encodes Def 5.5(1), and the book's remark p.116 says reflexive+symmetric is all that is needed.

definitions_mapped.coq: Record CN := mkCN {D :> DomCN; E : Equiv D}; Record CN_K := mkCN_K {D2 :> DomCN; E2 : Equiv_K D2} (l.13-16)
definitions_mapped.source: (5.13) CN as setoid; Def 5.5 pre-setoid; A7.9 pp. 200-201 verbatim (s.6.3.2 body text p.147 spells the fields B/B2 instead)
definitions_mapped.note: PHYINFO : CN_K (l.95) is built but consumed by no theorem; three_c refers to IC_PhyInfo directly. Probe: a generic `THREE_g (A:DomCN) (B:CN_K) (c:A->D2 B) P` over CN_K is definable and `three_c Book P <-> THREE_g Book PHYINFO bf P`.

definitions_mapped.coq: Parameter IC_Human : Equiv Human; Definition HUMAN := mkCN Human IC_Human (l.24-27)
definitions_mapped.source: (5.15) [human] = (Human, =h); s.6.3.2 p.147 verbatim

definitions_mapped.coq: Definition AIC_Man := fun x y : Man => IC_Human x y; Theorem EQ; Definition IC_Man := mkEquiv Man AIC_Man EQ; Definition MAN := mkCN Man IC_Man (l.30-39, 56-57)
definitions_mapped.source: (5.25) (=M) = (=H)|Man, realised as p.111 'given =H, we can define m =M m' as c(m) =H c(m')'; Def 5.2 sub-setoid MAN <| HUMAN; s.6.3.2 p.147 and A7.9 p.201-202 verbatim

definitions_mapped.coq: Definition three_f (A:CN) (P:A.(D)->Prop) := exists x, P x /\ exists y, P y /\ exists z, P z /\ ~E x y /\ ~E y z /\ ~E x z (l.43-45)
definitions_mapped.source: Def 5.3 Three_0(B, P) = exists x,y,z:B. D[B](x,y,z) /\ P x /\ P y /\ P z, D[B](x,y,z) = x <>_B y /\ y <>_B z /\ x <>_B z (5.27) p.112; A7.9 p.201 `three_0` renamed
definitions_mapped.note: Nested-existential form; probe lemma three_f_flat shows it is logically equivalent to the source's flat conjunction. Only Three_0 (the B = A case) is encoded; Def 5.4 Three(A, B, P) with A <= B is not.

definitions_mapped.note: `one` is a byte-for-byte duplicate of `some` (probe: `one A P = some A P` by reflexivity); added, used only in threedf.

definitions_mapped.coq: Parameters Phy : DomCN; Parameter Info : DomCN; Record PhyInfo : DomCN := mkPhyInfo {p :> Phy; i :> Info}; Parameter Book : DomCN; Axiom bf : Book -> PhyInfo; Coercion bf (l.71-79)

definitions_mapped.note: A plain product record with both projections declared as coercions stands in for the dot-type constructor. The formation side-condition C(A) cap C(B) = empty (Def 5.1, p.105) and a general A . B constructor are not encoded, so PHY . PHY would be formable. Coq's coercion chain Book >-> PhyInfo >-> Phy/Info reproduces Book <= PHY.INFO <= PHY, INFO (probe: `Print copred_dd2` with Set Printing Coercions shows `p (bf x)`, `i (bf x)`).

definitions_mapped.source: PHY = (PHY, =p) p.112, INFO = (INFO, =i) p.114; s.6.3.2 p.148 and A7.9 p.202 verbatim

definitions_mapped.coq: Definition AIC_PhyInfo a1 b1 := IC_Phy (p a1) (p b1) \/ IC_Info (i a1) (i b1); Theorem EQ1 (refl /\ sym); Definition IC_PhyInfo := mkEquiv_K PhyInfo AIC_PhyInfo EQ1; Definition PHYINFO := mkCN_K PhyInfo IC_PhyInfo (l.87-95)
definitions_mapped.source: Def 5.5(2) kappa_{A.B}(a1,b1,a2,b2) = kappa_A(a1,a2) \/ kappa_B(b1,b2) p.115; s.6.3.2 p.148 and A7.9 p.202 verbatim

definitions_mapped.coq: AIC_Book1/AIC_Book2 (restrict IC_Phy/IC_Info along bf), EQ2/EQ3, IC_Book1/IC_Book2, BOOK1 := mkCN Book IC_Book1, BOOK2 := mkCN Book IC_Book2 (l.98-120)
definitions_mapped.source: (5.43) BOOK1 = (Book, =p), (5.44) BOOK2 = (Book, =i) p.114; A7.9 p.203 verbatim

definitions_mapped.coq: Parameter picked_up : Human -> Phy -> Prop; Parameter mastered : Human -> Info -> Prop (l.122-123)
definitions_mapped.source: pick up : Human -> PHY -> Prop, master : Human -> INFO -> Prop (p.104, p.115); A7.9 p.203 verbatim

definitions_mapped.coq: Definition three_c (A:DomCN) (P:PhyInfo->Prop) := exists x y z : Book, ~IC_PhyInfo x y /\ ~IC_PhyInfo y z /\ ~IC_PhyInfo x z /\ P x /\ P y /\ P z (l.125-128)
definitions_mapped.source: Def 5.6 THREE(A, B, P) = exists x,y,z:A. D[B](x,y,z) /\ P x /\ P y /\ P z, B a pre-setoid with A <= B, D[B](x,y,z) = ~kappa_B(x,y) /\ ~kappa_B(y,z) /\ ~kappa_B(x,z) (p.116); (5.47) THREE(Book, PHY.INFO, pm(j)); A7.9 p.203 `three` renamed
definitions_mapped.note: Monomorphic instance: it quantifies over Book and uses IC_PhyInfo regardless of its argument A, which is a phantom (probe: `three_c nat P <-> three_c Book P` closes by `reflexivity`; `Check three_c nat` and `Check three_c Human` both type-check). The book's own `three` in A7.9 has the same phantom. The generic THREE needs A <= B as a hypothesis, which Coq's coercive subtyping cannot supply as a term; probe shows the explicit-coercion `THREE_g A B c P` is definable and coincides with three_c Book for c = bf.

definitions_mapped.coq: Definition and (A:DomCN) (P Q : A -> Prop) (x:A) := P x /\ Q x (l.130-131)
definitions_mapped.source: polymorphic conjunction and : Pi A:LType. A -> A -> A instantiated at Book -> Prop / PHY.INFO -> Prop (p.107, (5.12); Appendix 4); A7.9 p.203 verbatim
definitions_mapped.note: Specialised to predicate conjunction over A -> Prop. Shadows the identifier `and` of Coq.Init.Logic for indi and every file that Requires it (probe: `Print and` shows this definition; `Locate "/\\"` still gives Logic.and, so the notation is unaffected). The application `and PhyInfo (picked_up John) (mastered John)` elaborates by eta-expanding coercion insertion to `and PhyInfo (fun x => picked_up John (p x)) (fun x => mastered John (i x))` (verified with Set Printing Coercions), which is the book's contravariant step PHY -> Prop <= PHY.INFO -> Prop (p.105/p.107, lines 4971-4972 of the extracted text).

theorems.name: threedf (l.247-249)
theorems.source_claim: new; three_f PHY OTS -> one PHY OTS ('three physical objects on the shelf' implies 'one is'), loosely motivated by the (5.69)-(5.71) 'one/two/three books are on the shelf' discussion of s.5.4
theorems.note: Trivial (drop two witnesses). Print Assumptions: Phy, OTS, IC_Phy. Not in A7.9.

evidence: Lines 1-236 reproduce the book's Appendix A7.9 'Individuation' (pp. 200-207) essentially token-for-token: identical records Equiv/Equiv_K/CN/CN_K (l.6-16 = A7.9 pp. 200-201), identical ontology and coercion axioms mh/bf (l.19-21, 71-79 = pp. 201-202), identical AIC_*/IC_*/setoid definitions, identical proof scripts (e.g. `cbv. destruct IC_Human. destruct _eq4. destruct H0. ...` at l.36-39 = A7.9 p.201). The differences are the renamings three_0 -> three_f (l.43) and three -> three_c (l.125), five appendix comments dropped ('PhyInfo equiv is only reflexive and symmetric', 'The _K partial equivalence is used for PhyInfo', 'Double distinctness case', 'Double distinctness with conclusion expanded from the start', 'More than one adjectives and individuation') and one added (l.70).

19 of the file's 20 theorems are the book's, with the same statements and tactics; copred_dd2 (l.138-145) is additionally printed verbatim in s.6.3.2 pp. 148-149, and MANWALK (l.60-66) is (6.4) p.147 / (5.26) p.111.

Def 5.5(2) is encoded exactly as the disjunction AIC_PhyInfo (l.87-88) with the reflexive+symmetric proof EQ1 (l.90-92), and copred_dd1 (l.133-136) verifies the chapter's central double-distinctness claim (6.3)/(5.47)-(5.48) with no admits and no propositional axioms (Print Assumptions lists only Parameters and the two function-typed coercion axioms mh, bf).

The generic THREE of Def 5.6 is not encoded generically: three_c (l.125-128) hard-codes Book and IC_PhyInfo and its argument A is a phantom (probe: `three_c nat P <-> three_c Book P` by reflexivity). This simplification is the book's own (A7.9 p.203 `three`).

The adjective cases (5.54)/(5.55)/(5.60) are verified only in weakened single-IC form (HEAVYBOOK2/3, HEAVYIBOOK3-5, l.184-236), exactly as in A7.9 pp. 205-207; HEAVYIBOOK2 (l.222-224) duplicates HEAVYBOOK2, as in A7.9 p.206.
Heavyinfobook (l.193-194) nests Sigma(Sigma(Book, heavy), informative), reversing (5.58) HIBook = Sigma(IBook, heavy); A7.9 p.205 has the same order as the file.

The tail l.238-249 (OTS/WL/WaP, `one`, threedf) is the file's own addition: the two `Check`s type the s.5.4 formula (5.79) but prove nothing; `one` duplicates `some`; threedf is a trivial new theorem.
omissions: Def 5.4 generic Three(A, B, P) with A <= B and Def 5.6 generic THREE over arbitrary pre-setoids (only Three_0 and one monomorphic Book/IC_PhyInfo instance).
Def 5.2 sub-setoid relation <| as a definable predicate (only per-instance witnesses EQ, EQ2-EQ7).
Def 5.1 / Appendix 6 dot-type formation rule with the component non-sharing condition; a general A . B constructor (only PhyInfo).
(5.45) verb-domain-determined IC selection as an operation.
Double-distinctness premises for the adjective cases (5.54)/(5.55)/(5.60).
s.5.4 (5.80) with WO; the local-coercion context-dependence of the informational IC (p.123).
additions: Parameters OTS, WL, WaP and two `Check`s for (5.79) (l.238-245), unproved.

determination_rationale: The CNs-as-setoids theory of ch.5 encodes almost directly: setoids and pre-setoids as records with a coercion field, IC inheritance along a coercion (5.25), Sigma-types for adjectival modification (5.52)/(5.58), the disjunctive kappa for dot-types (Def 5.5) and the resulting double-distinctness derivation (5.47)-(5.48) all go through with 0 admits and 0 propositional axioms, and the book itself supplies this Coq code (A7.9). Three local adjustments are nevertheless forced by Coq: (a) no user-definable universe, so the CN-domain universe becomes Set (fn 12 p.142) and any Set is a CN domain; (b) coercive subtyping A <= B is not a first-class hypothesis, so the generic THREE(A, B, P) of Def 5.6 cannot be stated as written -- one either instantiates per pair (the file's and the book's choice, leaving a phantom argument in three_c) or threads an explicit coercion function (probe shows this works and is equivalent); (c) dot-types are not native, so PHY . INFO is simulated by a record with two `:>` projections and the formation side-condition of Def 5.1 is unenforced (the book concedes 'for types PHY and INFO only', p.148). A fourth, mechanical cost is that every sub-setoid needs its own equivalence proof (eight EQ lemmas). None of these changes the theory's structure, so the verdict is slight_modification rather than as_is.

artifact_classes.description: Universe collapse: `Definition DomCN := Set` (l.3) identifies the universe of CN domains with Set, so any Set is a common-noun domain and the book's separate universe CN (s.2.3.2, fn 12 p.142) is not represented. Verified: `Check three_c nat` and `Check three_c Human` both type-check as `(PhyInfo -> Prop) -> Prop`.

Missing native structure, two instances. (1) Coercive subtyping is not a first-class judgment in Coq, so Def 5.4/5.6's generic Three/THREE(A, B, P) 'for A <= B' cannot be written as stated; the file's three_c (l.125-128) hard-codes Book and IC_PhyInfo, its `A : DomCN` parameter is inert (probe: `three_c nat P <-> three_c Book P` by reflexivity), and the sub-setoid relation of Def 5.2 exists only as eight per-instance proofs (EQ, EQ1-EQ7). (2) Dot-types A . B with the component-non-sharing formation rule (Def 5.1, Appendix 6) are not native; PhyInfo (l.76-77) is an ordinary record with two `:>` projections, so the constraint is unenforced and only this one dot-type exists. Contravariant function subtyping (p.105) is recovered by Coq's eta-expanding coercion insertion (verified: `and PhyInfo (picked_up John) (mastered John)` elaborates to `and PhyInfo (fun x => picked_up John (p x)) (fun x => mastered John (i x))`), which happens to match the theory.
